content.content:
# Foliage

## Description

Foliage is built on the skeleton's leaf points, so leaves sit where the branches put them, and is shaded and animated so a crown reads as a volume of leaves.

## Clusters

- Each leaf point gets a cluster of alpha-tested cards, rotated around the branch by the golden angle, about 137.5 degrees, from its neighbour.
- Conifer clusters are needle sprays along the twig; broadleaf clusters are leaf cards splayed from the twig tip.

## Alpha

- Leaf textures use coverage-preserving mipmaps. Each mip level's alpha is scaled so the share of texels passing the alpha test matches the full-size texture, so crowns do not thin out or fade away with distance.
- The alpha-test threshold is one fixed value shared by every level and pass, the shadow pass included.
- Where the renderer has MSAA, foliage uses alpha-to-coverage, so card edges do not shimmer.

## Shading

- Card normals are blended with the normal of the crown's fitted ellipsoid, so the crown shades as one soft volume and the individual cards do not show.
- Leaves are two-sided and let light through, so a crown against a low sun glows at its edges.
- Ambient occlusion is baked per vertex from how deep a cluster sits inside the crown.
- Each instance gets a hue and value variation from its seed, within its species palette.

## Wind

- Sway is hierarchical: the trunk bends, each branch sways about its parent with an amplitude that grows with branch order, and leaves flutter.
- Each vertex carries its branch order, its phase and its distance along its branch, baked from the skeleton, and the motion is computed on the GPU from those and a global wind direction and strength.
- The impostor sways as a whole with the trunk motion, so it matches the geometry at the transition.
# Lod

## Description

Every variant has four levels of detail built from the same skeleton, and changing level is a cross-fade, never a swap.

## Levels

- LOD0 is the full skeleton: tapered branch tubes whose radial segment count falls with branch order, with every leaf cluster as foliage cards.
- LOD1 prunes the lowest prune priority segments until the segment count halves. The leaf clusters of a pruned subtree merge into one larger card at the point where it left the remaining branch, so foliage area and crown outline stay close to LOD0. The merged cards use the same leaf texture at the same texel density, the same crown-blended normals and the same colour as the clusters they replace, so the foliage does not visibly change texture, size or shade when the tree changes level.
- LOD2 keeps only the trunk and the first-order limbs. Foliage is a few large crown cards fitted to the clusters of each limb.
- LOD3 is an octahedral impostor baked from LOD0, with albedo, normal and depth, so it is lit by the same sun as the geometry.

## Nesting

The levels are nested, so every segment in a coarser level is also in every finer one, in the same place and at the same radius.

## Selection

- The level is chosen by the tree's projected height on screen, not by raw distance, so a change of camera field of view, as between the chase and the bonnet camera, picks the right level.
- Projected height is measured from the tree's bounding sphere and the camera's position and field of view before camera shake and bounce are applied, so a shaking camera does not push trees back and forth across a threshold.
- Each threshold has hysteresis. A tree moves to a coarser level when it drops below the threshold, and back to the finer one only when it rises above the threshold by a margin, 15% of the threshold by default.
- The default thresholds are pushed far out, so a player near a tree only ever sees it at full detail. A tree moves from LOD0 to LOD1 below 6% of the screen height, from LOD1 to LOD2 below 2.5% and from LOD2 to the impostor below 1%. For a 15 m tree at a 60 degree vertical field of view, that is roughly 215 m, 520 m and 1300 m.
- A tree within 120 m of the camera is always drawn at LOD0, whatever its projected height, the field of view or the graphics quality setting.
- Selection runs once per frame per tree and depends only on that frame's camera, never on draw order, culling batches or which pass is drawing.

## Transition

- A fade starts when the selected level changes and runs over a fixed time, 0.3 seconds by default, independent of frame rate and of how far the camera moves during it. It does not depend on where the tree is inside a distance band, so a car stopping near a threshold does not leave trees half faded.
- Each tree keeps its own fade state, the outgoing level, the incoming level and a fade value from 0 to 1, from frame to frame. A culled tree keeps its state, and a tree that comes into view takes its selected level at once with no fade.
- Both levels draw with the same screen-space dither mask and the same fade value. The outgoing level keeps the pixels whose mask value is at or above the fade value and the incoming level keeps those below it, so each pixel of the tree is covered by exactly one level and the tree is never thinner or more transparent than a solid tree at any point of the fade.
- Both levels are alpha-tested and write depth. A tree is never alpha-blended or drawn with a global opacity, so it never looks see-through while fading.
- If the selected level changes back during a fade, the fade reverses from its current value; it never restarts from 0 or snaps. A request for a third level waits until the running fade finishes.
- The dither mask is a fixed pattern anchored to screen pixels. It is not animated from frame to frame, and it is not jittered with temporal anti-aliasing unless the renderer's TAA resolves that jitter, so it does not shimmer or crawl.
- Wind sway and colour variation are the same on both levels during the fade, so nothing jumps when it ends.
- The impostor blends the three baked views nearest the view direction by their barycentric weights, so it does not jump from view to view as the camera passes the tree.

## Shadows

- Shadows use one level coarser than the one drawn, and never the impostor within the near shadow cascade.
- Shadow casters are never dithered. A tree's shadow level switches once, when its fade finishes, so its shadow does not flicker while the tree fades.

## Budget

The thresholds, the hysteresis margin and the fade time are per species, with defaults, and the thresholds can be scaled by the graphics quality setting. Lower quality settings may bring the thresholds closer, but never inside the 120 m full-detail distance.

## Debug View

A debug toggle tints each tree by the level it draws, shows trees in a fade with the fade value, and marks trees that changed level more than twice in the last second, so flickering trees can be found in a running stage.

content.text:
I can't give you a measured number. The project has no benchmark or frame-time data for trees, and `node_modules` isn't installed, so I couldn't build the meshes to count them. The figures below are estimates from the code, and the per-tree ones are rough.

**Per tree (LOD0)**
- **Branches:** the species allow up to 1,600–1,800 branch segments (`species.ts`). Each is a tube with 8 sides at the trunk down to 3 on the thinnest twigs (`mesh.ts:77`). That's roughly 8–10k triangles.
- **Leaves:** nearly every segment ends in a leaf point with 3–4 cards of 2 triangles each. That's another 8–12k triangles.
- **Total:** roughly 15–20k triangles per tree at full detail. The vegetation budget in `assets/library.ts:180` caps a whole set of variants at 1,200 triangles, which suggests the vegetation it was sized for was a few hundred triangles each. So each nearby tree is probably 10–50× heavier than before.

**Per frame**
- The spec makes every tree within 120 m LOD0, whatever the quality setting, and the code agrees (`FULL_DETAIL_DISTANCE`). A forest stage can have 100+ trees in that range, the case that code comment warns about. That's on the order of 1.5–2M triangles in the main pass.
- The shadow pass adds about half that again, because shadows use the next coarser level (LOD1), which has half the segments.
- Trees are drawn in instanced batches, one per variant, level and part, so draw calls stay modest. The cost is in vertex work and pixel shading, not draw calls.

**Pixel cost, probably the bigger hit on weaker GPUs**
- Leaves are alpha-tested (they throw away transparent pixels), double-sided and stacked several cards deep. Throwing pixels away (`discard`) stops the GPU from skipping hidden pixels early, so a dense crown shades the same screen area many times over.
- Alpha-to-coverage adds a cost with MSAA on.
- The fade between detail levels adds a `discard` to every tree pixel (`materials.ts:149`), not just to leaves.

**Where it gets cheaper:** trees only drop below full detail at about 215 m, 520 m and 1,300 m for a 15 m tree. Distant trees are cheap, but the near band is where the cost sits, and you can't lower it from the quality setting because the 120 m rule is in the spec.

To get real numbers, run a forest stage and compare frame time and triangle count against an older build. The game's `StatsOverlay` and the `?treedebug=1` level tinting will show how many trees sit at LOD0. I can work out the exact triangle counts per species and level from `mesh.ts` if you'd like.

**Per frame**
- The spec makes every tree within 120 m LOD0, whatever the quality setting, and the code agrees (`FULL_DETAIL_DISTANCE`). A forest stage can have 100+ trees in that range, the case that code comment warns about. That's on the order of 1.5–2M triangles in the main pass.
- The shadow pass adds about half that again, because shadows use the next coarser level (LOD1), which has half the segments.
- Trees are drawn in instanced batches, one per variant, level and part, so draw calls stay modest. The cost is in vertex work and pixel shading, not draw calls.

**Pixel cost, probably the bigger hit on weaker GPUs**
- Leaves are alpha-tested (they throw away transparent pixels), double-sided and stacked several cards deep. Throwing pixels away (`discard`) stops the GPU from skipping hidden pixels early, so a dense crown shades the same screen area many times over.
- Alpha-to-coverage adds a cost with MSAA on.
- The fade between detail levels adds a `discard` to every tree pixel (`materials.ts:149`), not just to leaves.

**Where it gets cheaper:** trees only drop below full detail at about 215 m, 520 m and 1,300 m for a 15 m tree. Distant trees are cheap, but the near band is where the cost sits, and you can't lower it from the quality setting because the 120 m rule is in the spec.

To get real numbers, run a forest stage and compare frame time and triangle count against an older build. The game's `StatsOverlay` and the `?treedebug=1` level tinting will show how many trees sit at LOD0. I can work out the exact triangle counts per species and level from `mesh.ts` if you'd like.
